lstNewsbyCategory.title: India allows import of 6,500 tonnes of silver amid sluggish demand
lstNewsbyCategory.content: India has issued permits to import around 6,500 metric tons of silver over the next six months to meet festive-season demand, despite recent import restrictions and increased duties from 6% to 15%. The move is expected to lower domestic silver premiums, which dropped to 45 cents per ounce, while overall demand remains subdued.

lstNewsbyCategory.title: Gold steady after 3% fall sparked by Warsh's hawkish comments
lstNewsbyCategory.content: Gold prices were steady at $4,455.29 per ounce after a more than 3% drop, following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s signal that the interest rate hikes may be needed to control inflation. Market odds of a September rate hike rose to 57%. Silver held at $66.34, platinum at $1,822.46, and palladium at $1,424.89.

lstNewsbyCategory.title: Indian jewellery stocks drop up to 4% amid gold, silver import changes
lstNewsbyCategory.content: The Centre increased import duty on gold, silver, and other precious metals by 10% to 15%. This move makes precious metal imports costlier, weighing on sector sentiment. Kalyan Jewellers declined 4.33%, while Titan Company slipped 0.43%. Domestic bullion prices surged, with gold prices on MCX hitting a 6% upper circuit at Rs 1.62 lakh per 10 grams, and silver prices at Rs 2.95 lakh per kg.

lstNewsbyCategory.title: Oil surge, Iran war fears drive up gold, silver prices sharply
lstNewsbyCategory.content: Gold and silver prices opened sharply lower on the Multi-Commodity Exchange of India on Friday. MCX silver futures fell 1% to Rs 2,39,200 per kg, while gold futures declined 0.4% to Rs 1,51,159 per 10 grams, due to surging oil prices and escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Globally, spot gold edged up 0.1% to $4,697 per ounce, despite a weekly decline.
